newsitem.title: USA: Pilots call for anti-collision equipment.
newsitem.headline: Pilots call for anti-collision equipment.

text.p: The Independent Pilots Association called on Wednesday for anti-collision equipment to be installed aboard cargo aircraft, after a plane was involved in a close encounter with Air Force One during President Bill Clinton's flight to Europe last week.

Captain Dom Devito, who was flying a United Parcel Service plane which came within two to four miles of Clinton's aircraft off the coast of Ireland last Monday, said the incident showed how dangerous it was to fly without the equipment.
A sensitive anti-collision system, the Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), advised the crew of Air Force One, a Boeing 747, that the UPS aircraft was below them and descending.
Devito said he had no idea another plane was close by until he was ordered by an air traffic controller to take evasive action.
"I'd like to meet the President but I didn't want to run into him this way," he said.
Federal regulations require the anti-collision system on all aircraft carrying 10 or more passengers, but not on cargo planes.
Devito said his plane was descending from 31,000 feet to 28,000 feet when he was advised by an air traffic controller at Ireland's Shannon Airport to turn to the left.
The controller also told the pilot of Air Force One, who was travelling in the opposite direction at 28,000 feet, to turn and to climb to a higher altitude.
The two planes were seven seconds flying time apart at the time, but it was not clear if they were on a collision course.

"We should have TCAS on board. Perhaps if we did have TCAS on board, it would have avoided a close incident and we would not have not depend on Shannon control for our evasive maneuvers," Devito said.
The Air Force said on Tuesday Clinton was never in any danger.
Fleet Smith, a pilot who investigated the incident for the Pilots Association, said Congress should close a loophole in the law that allowed cargo aircraft to fly without TCAS.
"I believe this points out the need for collision avoidance devices on all large cargo jets in the interests of the safety of the pilots and also the travelling public," he said.
